subject: When loading in the data the number of features is a 100 fold less than expected

messages.author: 3b0927e3433901fb
messages.subject: When loading in the data the number of features is a 100 fold less than expected
parts:
Hi there,

When loading in my dataset there are only around 500 features picked up by the package. I am expecting >50,000 prior to normalisation.

Any ideas on how I can sort this? 
At the moment I am loading the data in using the readImzML function.

Thanks in advance, 
Daria

messages.author: 85065719d208a2af
messages.subject: Re: When loading in the data the number of features is a 100 fold less than expected
parts:
Hi Daria, 
I can recommend two things. 

1) Generate a minimal reproducible example so that one can reproduce your problem and possibly come up with a straight forward answer. 
2) While reading your dataset (say imzML) try feeding resolution parameter to your file import call. 

Example: 

{ # read imzML file using Cardinal.
MSI_DatasetName <- Cardinal::readImzML("FileName",   # don't write extension, also put the file in the same dir.                  
                    resolution = 20,
                    units = "ppm",
                    as = "MSImagingExperiment",
                    attach.only = T)
}
Best, 
Shad
